title: California Vacation Accrual Policy (Synthetic)
text: Full-time employees in California accrue paid vacation at a rate of twenty days per calendar year. Accrued vacation is treated as earned wages and vests as it is earned. An employer may impose a reasonable cap on total accrued vacation, but a strict use-it-or-lose-it policy that forfeits earned vacation is not permitted. Upon separation of employment, all accrued and unused vacation must be paid out at the employee's final rate of pay. Employers may lawfully cap carryover of unused vacation at a maximum of five days into the following calendar year, provided the cap is applied prospectively and communicated in writing. Sick leave is governed separately and is not subject to these accrual and payout rules.

title: Federal Paid Sick Leave Guidance (Synthetic)
text: Covered employees receive ten paid sick days per year for personal illness, medical appointments, or the care of an immediate family member. Paid sick leave is distinct from paid vacation and may not be substituted for vacation payout upon termination. Unused sick days do not vest as wages and are not paid out at separation unless a collective bargaining agreement provides otherwise. Employers may require reasonable documentation for absences exceeding three consecutive workdays. Retaliation against an employee for lawfully using sick leave is prohibited and may give rise to civil penalties.

title: Nguyen v. Pacific Logistics (Synthetic)
text: The plaintiff, a logistics coordinator, alleged wrongful denial of a remote-work accommodation. The company policy permitted employees to work remotely up to three days per week subject to manager approval. The court held that where an employer grants discretionary remote-work privileges, it must apply approval criteria consistently and may not deny requests on the basis of a protected characteristic. Because the employer approved comparable requests from similarly situated employees while denying the plaintiff's, the court found the denial pretextual. The ruling clarifies that a discretionary remote-work policy does not create an unconditional right to work remotely, but it does require even-handed application of the stated approval standard.

title: Alvarez v. Hudson Retail Group (Synthetic)
text: The plaintiffs, a class of retail associates, sued for unpaid overtime. New York law requires overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours worked beyond forty in a workweek for non-exempt employees. The employer argued the associates were exempt executives, but the court applied the duties test and found the employees spent the majority of their time on non-exempt tasks such as stocking shelves and operating registers. The court held that an employee's job title does not determine exemption; the actual duties performed control. Misclassification exposed the employer to back pay plus liquidated damages.

title: Internal HR Memo: Combined PTO Rollover (Synthetic)
text: This memo summarizes the company's paid-time-off rollover rules for the 2024-2025 cycle. Employees may carry over a maximum of five unused vacation days into the next calendar year; any excess is forfeited on December 31 unless prohibited by state law. In California, forfeiture of earned vacation is not permitted, so California employees instead reach an accrual cap at which further accrual pauses until the balance is drawn down. Sick leave does not roll over and does not pay out at separation. Managers should direct employees with balances above the cap to schedule time off before year-end.

title: Data Retention for Employee Records (Synthetic)
text: Personal data of employees must be processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently. Employee records may be retained only for as long as necessary for the purposes for which they were collected, such as payroll, tax compliance, and the administration of leave balances. Once an employee leaves and all legal retention obligations have lapsed, records containing personal data must be deleted or anonymized. Employees have the right to access their personal data and to request correction of inaccurate information. Cross-border transfers of employee data outside the European Economic Area require an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards.
